question.text: What will be Lake Mead’s elevation at the end of November 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the value in feet for November 2026 presented by the Bureau of Reclamation at its [LAKE MEAD AT HOOVER DAM, END OF MONTH ELEVATION (FEET)](https://www.usbr.gov/lc/region/g4000/hourly/mead-elv.html) data set.
question.fine_print: This question will not re-resolve based on future revisions.

research:
I could not find anything that settles this yet. The last official value is 1,038.85 ft at the end of October 2026, and the lake was at about 1,039.2-1,039.3 ft on Nov 3-4. The October Reclamation study expects a drop of about 1.3 ft from October to November, but October ended about 3.5 ft above that study's forecast. Over 2015-2025, the October-to-November change usually ran between -0.8 and +1.3 ft.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-05: Reclamation's table lists end-of-month values for 2026: Jun 1044.58, Jul 1041.10, Aug 1038.83, Sep 1037.80, **Oct 1038.85**. November 2026 is not posted yet. [USBR](https://www.usbr.gov/lc/region/g4000/hourly/mead-elv.html)
- The same table shows November values of 1060.89 in 2024 and 1058.91 in 2025. [USBR](https://www.usbr.gov/lc/region/g4000/hourly/mead-elv.html)

## 2. Current status
- 2026-11-04: Lake Mead was at 1,039.29 ft (provisional), up 0.08 ft in a day and 0.91 ft in a week. [Hydrostatus](https://hydrostatus.com/lake-mead/)
- 2026-11-03: Daily readings rose every day: Oct 28 at 1,038.38, Oct 31 at 1,038.85, Nov 1 at 1,038.93, Nov 2 at 1,039.06, Nov 3 at 1,039.21. The recent low was 1,037.16 on Oct 22. [LakeProjections](https://www.lakeprojections.com/lake-mead/water-level)
- 2026-11-03: That site's own daily forecast (not an official one) has the lake easing to 1,038.72 by Nov 30, then rising to 1,040.38 by Dec 31. [LakeProjections](https://www.lakeprojections.com/lake-mead/water-level)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-05: Reports describe the strongest El Niño on record. A storm last weekend killed at least four people and brought Arizona two to three months of rain in a few days. I have not checked whether that runoff reaches Mead. [AlterNet](https://www.alternet.org/el-nino-2026-2678297108/)
- 2026-11-04: NOAA and FOX Weather give an 83% chance that this becomes the strongest El Niño since 1950. A stormy pattern is expected across the southern US this winter. [FOX Weather](https://www.foxweather.com/weather-news/regions-super-el-nino-benefit-california-southwest-texas-fall-winter-2026)
- 2026-10-30: According to Autonocion, Reclamation's Oct 26 weekly sheet shows 5.78 in of precipitation in the Mead basin since Oct 1, 465% of normal. The 24-Month Study assumed 71 kaf of October inflow, but the river forecast center projects 120 kaf (147% of average). Lake Powell rose 6.96 ft in a week to 3,527.51 ft. [Autonocion](https://www.autonocion.com/us/726-foot-dam-three-feet-1035-line-lake-mead-weekly-sheet-year-end/)
- Late Oct 2026: Lake Mead has risen about 11 in from a record low to roughly 1,038 ft, but the long-term outlook is still dire. [KGUN9](https://www.kgun9.com/news/state/lake-mead-and-lake-powell-water-levels-rising-in-october-but-long-term-outlook-remains-dire)
- Oct 2026: Rain from Tropical Storm Rachel raised Mead only about 0.1 ft. [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/why-tropical-storm-rachel-drenching-barely-touches-lake-mead-water-crisis-12561921)
- 2026-10-17: In the October 24-Month Study's most probable case, Mead ends Oct at 1,035.29, Nov at **1,033.97** and Dec at 1,034.52. I only have this from a secondary source; I could not read the PDF to confirm the November figure. Actual October came in at 1,038.85, about 3.56 ft above the study. If the study's Oct-to-Nov change (-1.32 ft) is applied to the actual October value, November would be about 1,037.5. That is my arithmetic, not a forecast. [Autonocion](https://www.autonocion.com/us/726-foot-dam-17-turbines-lake-mead-1035-feet-november-317-megawatts/), [USBR 24-Month Study](https://www.usbr.gov/lc/region/g4000/24mo_6.pdf)

## 4. Base rates
October-to-November changes in end-of-month elevation, from the [USBR table](https://www.usbr.gov/lc/region/g4000/hourly/mead-elv.html):

| Year | Change (ft) |
|---|---|
| 2015 | -0.76 |
| 2016 | +0.21 |
| 2017 | -1.35 |
| 2018 | -0.20 |
| 2019 | +1.24 |
| 2020 | -0.81 |
| 2021 | -1.80 |
| 2022 | -3.26 |
| 2023 | -0.53 |
| 2024 | -0.33 |
| 2025 | +1.34 |

- The median change is about -0.5 ft. The range is -3.26 to +1.34, and most years fall between -0.8 and +1.3.
- Adding those changes to October's 1,038.85 gives a historical range of about 1,035.6 to 1,040.2, centered near 1,038.3.
- For context, the July 2026 model runs (30 scenarios, not probabilities) put Dec 1, 2026 between 1,032.29 and 1,043.87. [LakeProjections](https://www.lakeprojections.com/lake-mead/projections)

## 5. Other forecasts
- **Kalshi, "Lake Mead end-of-month elevation next month (Dec 2026)":** Yes prices are above 1033 at 0.95, above 1034 at 0.88, above 1035 at 0.74, above 1036 at 0.74, above 1037 at 0.70, above 1038 at 0.56, above 1039 at 0.47 and above 1040 at 0.38. That implies a median around 1,038.5-1,039. I could not confirm whether this contract settles on the November end-of-month value (published in December) or the December one, so check the contract rules.
- **Polymarket, "How low will Lake Mead drop?" (through 2027-04-16):** This asks for the minimum through April, not the November value. Below 1,028 is 0.32, 1,028-1,033 is 0.48, 1,033-1,038 is 0.24 and above 1,038 is 0.05.
- **Reclamation's October Most Probable:** 1,033.97 for end of November (secondary source, see section 3).

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Around mid-November 2026: the November 24-Month Study, reportedly due about Nov 15, will update the Nov and Dec projections. [USBR](https://www.usbr.gov/lc/region/g4000/24mo_6.pdf)
- Weekly Reclamation hydrologic updates, published on Mondays. [USBR weekly](https://www.usbr.gov/lc/region/g4000/weekly.pdf)
- More El Niño storms could raise Virgin River and side inflows. Hoover releases and downstream demand usually fall in November and December, which helps hold the level up.
- Lake Powell's monthly release volume for November (I did not find the number).
- The official November value should be posted around Dec 1.

Sources: [USBR mead-elv](https://www.usbr.gov/lc/region/g4000/hourly/mead-elv.html), [USBR 24mo_6](https://www.usbr.gov/lc/region/g4000/24mo_6.pdf), [USBR weekly](https://www.usbr.gov/lc/region/g4000/weekly.pdf), [Hydrostatus](https://hydrostatus.com/lake-mead/), [LakeProjections level](https://www.lakeprojections.com/lake-mead/water-level), [LakeProjections projections](https://www.lakeprojections.com/lake-mead/projections), [Autonocion Oct 17](https://www.autonocion.com/us/726-foot-dam-17-turbines-lake-mead-1035-feet-november-317-megawatts/), [Autonocion Oct 30](https://www.autonocion.com/us/726-foot-dam-three-feet-1035-line-lake-mead-weekly-sheet-year-end/), [KGUN9](https://www.kgun9.com/news/state/lake-mead-and-lake-powell-water-levels-rising-in-october-but-long-term-outlook-remains-dire), [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/why-tropical-storm-rachel-drenching-barely-touches-lake-mead-water-crisis-12561921), [FOX Weather](https://www.foxweather.com/weather-news/regions-super-el-nino-benefit-california-southwest-texas-fall-winter-2026), [AlterNet](https://www.alternet.org/el-nino-2026-2678297108/)

- 2026-11-04: Reclamation's daily readings were Nov 1: 1038.93, Nov 2: 1039.06, Nov 3: 1039.21, **Nov 4: 1039.29 ft**. That is about +0.12 ft/day, and +0.44 ft since the end of October. [USBR levels](https://www.usbr.gov/lc/region/g4000/hourly/levels.html)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The lake is at about 1039.3 ft and rising after the late-October and early-November storms, with 26 days left in the month.
- 2026-10-22: Lake Mead hit its all-time low, about 1037.2 ft. Since then it has risen about 2 ft. [KTAR](https://ktar.com/arizona-water-news/lake-powell-lake-mead-levels-colorado)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-05: Reports describe the strongest El Niño on record. Last weekend's storm dropped 2 to 3 months' worth of rain on Arizona in a few days. I did not verify this beyond the article. [Alternet](https://www.alternet.org/el-nino-2026-2678297108/)
- 2026-11-04: Lake Powell reached 3,533 ft, up 17 ft from its mid-September low. Lake Mead is rising less because its level is driven mainly by releases from Powell. [KTAR](https://ktar.com/arizona-water-news/lake-powell-lake-mead-levels-colorado)
- 2026-11-04: NOAA and FOX Weather give an 83% chance this becomes the strongest El Niño since 1950, with a stormy southern-tier winter. [FOX Weather](https://www.foxweather.com/weather-news/regions-super-el-nino-benefit-california-southwest-texas-fall-winter-2026)
- 2026-10-27/28: A Reclamation spokesperson said Mead "is projected to end the months of October and November about 3 feet higher" than the October 24-Month Study showed. The reasons given were extra tributary inflow and lower irrigation demand in southern Arizona and California. [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/storms-relief-lake-powell-mead-record-low-12621062)
- 2026-10-26: The weekly sheet put Mead at 1038.03 ft on Oct 25, up 0.79 ft on the week. Precipitation in the Mead basin since Oct 1 was 5.78 in, 465% of normal. [Autonocion](https://www.autonocion.com/us/726-foot-dam-three-feet-1035-line-lake-mead-weekly-sheet-year-end/)
- 2026-10-15: The October 24-Month Study (most probable case, run Oct 8, before the storms) projected end-of-month levels of Oct 1035.29, **Nov 1033.97**, Dec 1034.52, Jan 1034.33 and Mar 1027.24 ft. Glen Canyon release for the water year is set at 6.0 million acre-feet. Secondary source; I could not read the official PDF. [Autonocion](https://www.autonocion.com/us/726-foot-dam-17-turbines-lake-mead-1035-feet-november-317-megawatts/), [probable min study](https://www.usbr.gov/lc/region/g4000/24mo_MIN.pdf), [probable max study](https://data.usbr.gov/rise/content-rise-public/rise/catalog-item/binary/OCT26_MAX_508.pdf)
- Implied numbers:
  - October actually ended 3.56 ft above the study's projection.
  - The study expected a Nov change of -1.32 ft. Applied to the actual October value, that gives about 1037.5.
  - The study's figure plus Reclamation's "about 3 ft higher" gives about 1037.
  - The daily data so far show a rise, not a fall.

## 4. Base rates
- End-of-October to end-of-November changes from the official table:
  - 2024: 1061.22 to 1060.89 (-0.33 ft).
  - 2025: 1057.57 to 1058.91 (+1.34 ft). [USBR](https://www.usbr.gov/lc/region/g4000/hourly/mead-elv.html)
- Recent month-to-month changes in the fall run about -1 to +1.5 ft. Lower Basin demand in November is low, so the level is usually flat to slightly rising heading into December.
- 2026 trend: steep decline Mar to Sep (about 1066 to 1037.8), a low in late October, and +1.05 ft in October.
- A simple extrapolation is very uncertain. If early November's +0.1 ft/day continued, the lake would end up near 1041 to 1042. Tributary storm runoff usually fades within days, though, and the study pattern points to a decline over the month.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi, "Lake Mead end-of-month elevation next month?", labeled Dec 2026: Above 1033: 0.95, 1034: 0.88, 1035: 0.74, 1036: 0.74, 1037: 0.70, 1038: 0.56, 1039: 0.47, 1040: 0.38.
  - "Next month" may mean the November end-of-month value; I could not confirm which month this market settles on.
  - Taken at face value, the market median is roughly 1038.5 to 1039.
- Polymarket, "How low will Lake Mead drop?" (ends 2027-04-16): this tracks the minimum through April 2027, not the end of November. Prices: below 1028: 0.32, 1028-1033: 0.48, 1033-1038: 0.24, above 1038: 0.05.
- Official guidance:
  - The October 24-Month Study shows Nov at 1033.97, but it is outdated.
  - Reclamation's verbal guidance (about 3 ft higher) implies about 1037.
  - Third-party sites such as [lakeprojections](https://www.lakeprojections.com/lake-mead/water-level) and [reservoirbench](https://reservoirbench.com/lake-mead/) have projections I did not verify.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Mid-November 2026: the November 24-Month Study is due, with an updated end-of-November projection that includes the storm inflows. [USBR 24-month](https://www.usbr.gov/lc/region/g4000/24mo.pdf)
- Weekly Lower Colorado hydrologic updates (Mondays). [USBR weekly](https://www.usbr.gov/lc/region/g4000/weekly.pdf)
- More El Niño storms could add tributary inflow (Virgin River, Las Vegas Wash) and further cut irrigation demand. A dry spell would let the lake drift down as Hoover releases continue.
- November releases from Glen Canyon and Hoover: I could not find the monthly volumes.
- Ongoing Colorado River post-2026 negotiations and litigation are unlikely to affect November levels.

forecasts.reasoning:
**(a) Time left:** About 25 days. The November value should be posted around Dec 1, 2026.

**(b) Latest known value:** The official end-of-October 2026 value is 1,038.85 ft. The provisional daily reading was 1,039.29 ft on Nov 4, still rising about 0.1 ft per day after the storm.

**(c) If nothing changed:** About 1,039.3 ft.

**(d) If the current trend continued:** Projecting the storm-driven rise forward naively gives about 1,041 to 1,042 ft. That is unlikely to hold, because side inflows taper after storms. Reclamation's typical November balance, where Hoover releases slightly exceed Powell releases, points to a small net decline. The October 24-Month Study had a -1.3 ft October-to-November change.

**(e) Historical variation:** Over 2015-2025 the October-to-November change had a median of about -0.5 ft. It ranged from -3.3 to +1.3 ft, and most years fell between -0.8 and +1.3 ft. Applied to 1,038.85, that gives a central estimate near 1,038.3, but the lake is already 0.44 ft higher in early November.

**(f) Experts and markets:**
- Kalshi's "next month" market implies a median of about 1,038.5 to 1,039 ft. It is unclear whether that contract settles on November or December.
- LakeProjections forecasts 1,038.72 ft for Nov 30.
- Reclamation's October Most Probable run of 1,033.97 ft is stale. October came in 3.5 ft above that study's forecast.

**(g) Scenarios:**
- **Low:** Storm inflows stop quickly, Hoover releases stay high, and the November 24-Month Study plan pulls the lake down about 2 to 3 ft (as in 2022), giving roughly 1,036 to 1,037 ft.
- **High:** Repeated strong El Niño storms over the Virgin River and Las Vegas Wash basins, plus higher Powell releases, give roughly 1,041 to 1,042 ft.

**Synthesis:** I anchor near 1,038.9 ft, between the current level and the typical seasonal decline.

**Tails:**
- **1st percentile:** A larger-than-usual November drawdown, with release volumes front-loaded and storm inflows ending, could reach about 1,035.5 ft.
- **99th percentile:** Repeated major storms could reach about 1,042.5 ft.

(b) **Latest known value:** The official end-of-October 2026 value is 1,038.85 ft. The provisional daily reading was 1,039.29 ft on November 4, 2026, and it has been rising daily since the October 22 low of 1,037.16.

(c) **If nothing changed:** About 1,039.3 ft.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** The lake has risen about 0.9 ft per week, driven by storm runoff into Mead. Continuing that for the rest of the month would give about 1,042 ft. That is unlikely, because storm inflows fade and Powell releases and downstream demand set the baseline. The more realistic path is a small further rise, then a slow drift down, ending near 1,038.7 to 1,039.2.

(e) **Historical variation:** From 2015 to 2025, the October-to-November change ranged from -3.26 ft to +1.34 ft, with a median of about -0.5 ft. Applied to 1,038.85, that gives a range of about 1,035.6 to 1,040.2. We already know the first 0.44 ft of November's move, which narrows the uncertainty somewhat.

(f) **Expert and market expectations:**
- Reclamation's October 24-Month Study implied about 1,034 ft, but it is stale: October came in 3.5 ft above it.
- Applying the study's Oct-to-Nov change to the actual October value gives about 1,037.5 ft.
- LakeProjections forecasts 1,038.72 ft for November 30.
- The Kalshi market, which likely covers this same November end-of-month value, implies a median of about 1,038.5 to 1,039. Its prices are illiquid and somewhat inconsistent.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** Storm inflows drop off quickly, and Reclamation or Powell operations raise net outflow, for example through higher Hoover releases for downstream deliveries or a reduced Powell release. The lake falls 2 to 3 ft from its early-November peak, ending near 1,036.
- **High:** The record El Niño brings repeated heavy storms to the lower basin in November, sustaining Virgin River and side inflows while demand stays low. The lake climbs to 1,041 or 1,042.
